paragraphs: Rabbi Avin the carpenter. Rav Huna passed his doorway, saw his care with the lamp, and said, “Two great men will issue from here”: Rav Idi and Rabbi Chiyya, Shabbat 23b. Because the man and his wife both took care, two issued (Tosafot likewise). Alternatively, they took care with the lamps—that is, the Shabbat lamp and the Chanukah lamp. This seems supported by the passage there: Rav Chisda habitually passed the door of Rav Shizvi’s father-in-law’s household, saw he was very regular with lamps, and said, “A great man will issue from here.” Rav Shizvi issued, etc. It does not use the plural “they were regular with lamps.” Midrash Shmuel, beginning of chapter 27: Rabbi Bon bar Nagri. (See above, Ivo bar Nagra.)
